To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have resolved the cold dust emission of the elliptical galaxy M86 and found that it is spatially coinciding with stripped material from a nearby spiral galaxy.

the Herschel-Spitzer observations of M 86 reveal three distinct dust components: emission associated with the central region, a dust lane extending along the north-south axis, and a bright emission region to the south-east; the dust emission associated with the gas component in the central region has a gas-to-dust mass ratio of similar to 20 to 80.
the dust morphology of M 86 is complex with three distinct features.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the origin of the dust and its distribution in M 86.
the dust morphology of the giant elliptic galaxy M 86 with Herschel-Spire.
(i) the origin of the dust and gas; (ii) the origin of dust heating; (iii) the origin of a dust ring; and (iv) a possible connection with the radio jet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dust morphology is a combination of the effects of the ram-pressure stripping of gas from NGC 4438, the tidal interaction with NGC 4438 and the interaction with the intracluster medium.

the dust in the central region and the north-south dust lane are heated by the old and young stellar populations, respectively; the dust in the south-eastern feature is heated by a combination of old and young stars, and the dust associated with stripped material from NGC 4438 is heated by young stars.
the dust is not a reliable tracer of the gas in the central regions of galaxies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dust in the central region of M 86 is heated by the central engine, the dust lane by the tidal interaction with NGC 4438, and the south-eastern feature by a combination of heating by a star-forming clump and the central engine.
the Herschel-Spire images of M 86 reveal a complex dust distribution that is not only related to the central region of the galaxy, but also to the tidal interaction with NGC 4438.
the dust in M 86 has a complex morphology and a variety of heating sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dust morphology of M 86 is not dominated by a central starburst, but rather by a combination of a central star formation and a tidal interaction with NGC 4438.
dust can survive tidal interactions and be spatially associated with the stripped material.
the dust emission is not always associated with the molecular gas and can be used as an additional tool to study the gas distribution in galaxies.
